Based on my search, I can provide you with information about the **Navy P-3** aircraft.

## Lockheed P-3 Orion

The **P-3 Orion** is a four-engine turboprop anti-submarine and maritime surveillance aircraft developed for the United States Navy by Lockheed Corporation. It was one of the most successful and longest-serving maritime patrol aircraft in history.

### Key Variants

| Variant | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **P-3A** | Initial production version (1962) |
| **P-3B** | Improved variant with upgraded engines and avionics |
| **P-3C** | Major upgrade with digital avionics, improved sensors, and weapons systems |
| **P-3C AIP** | Anti-Surface Warfare Improvement Program upgrade |
| **P-3C AIP+** | Further enhanced version with additional capabilities |
| **EP-3E** | Signals intelligence (SIGINT) variant |
| **WP-3D** | Weather reconnaissance variant for NOAA |
| **CP-140 Aurora** | Canadian variant |

### Key Specifications

| Feature | Specification |
|---------|-------------|
| Crew | 11-13 (pilot, copilot, flight engineer, navigator, tactical coordinator, sensor operators, etc.) |
| Length | 116 ft 10 in (35.6 m) |
| Wingspan | 99 ft 8 in (30.4 m) |
| Height | 33 ft 8.5 in (10.3 m) |
| Max Takeoff Weight | ~142,000 lb (64,400 kg) |
| Powerplant | 4 × Allison T56-A-14 turboprops |
| Max Speed | ~411 knots (473 mph, 761 km/h) |
| Range | ~2,380 nmi (4,400 km) |
| Endurance | ~16+ hours (loiter time) |

### Primary Missions

- **Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW)**
- **Anti-Surface Warfare (ASuW)**
- **Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR)**
- **Maritime Patrol**
- **Search and Rescue (SAR)**

### Operational History

- **Entered service**: 1962
- **Primary operator**: U.S. Navy patrol squadrons (VP squadrons)
- The P-3C remained the primary land-based maritime patrol aircraft for the U.S. Navy until being gradually replaced by the **P-8 Poseidon** (based on the Boeing 737)
- Many P-3s have been retired to **AMARG** (Aerospace Maintenance and Regeneration Group) at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base, Arizona
- Several aircraft have been transferred to foreign military sales or other government agencies (NASA, NOAA)

### Notable Features

- The P-3 is based on the **Lockheed L-188 Electra** commercial airliner
- Features a distinctive ** Magnetic Anomaly Detector (MAD)** boom extending from the tail
- Can carry a variety of weapons including torpedoes, depth charges, Harpoon anti-ship missiles, and mines in an internal bomb bay and on wing pylons
- The aircraft has been operated by numerous countries including Australia, Japan, Norway, Spain, Taiwan, and others

The P-3 Orion has had an exceptionally long service life, with some aircraft serving for over 50 years before retirement.

Sources:
1. https://www.p3orion.nl/ALHR.pdf
